title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: The study of the economy as a whole: overall output, prices and employment, and the policies that affect them.

en.text: Microeconomics studies individual agents; macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole — growth, unemployment, inflation, government deficits, exports, imports and the trade balance — and the two are complementary. Variables such as GDP, the unemployment rate and inflation measure a country's macroeconomic performance. Since the 1930s, classical and neoclassical, Keynesian, monetarist, new classical and new Keynesian schools of thought have shaped macroeconomics.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Microeconomics: individual households, workers and businesses.
Macroeconomics: the economy as a whole.
Focus areas: growth, employment, inflation, income distribution, policies, international trade.
GDP, the unemployment rate and inflation measure macroeconomic performance.
Schools since the 1930s: classical and neoclassical, Keynesian, monetarist, new classical, new Keynesian.

screens.title: Key formulas
paras: GDP = Σ Pᵢ Qᵢ; GNP = GDP + NFI.
GDP = C + I + G + NE, with NE = X − M.
Growth rate = (real GDPₜ − real GDPₜ₋₁) ÷ real GDPₜ₋₁ × 100.
CPI = (cost of basket now ÷ base-year cost) × 100.

items.text: There is no difference between microeconomics and macroeconomics.
items.why: Micro studies individual units; macro studies the economy as a whole. They differ but are complementary.

items.text: Macroeconomics focuses on the economy as a whole.

Microeconomic goals include achieving high economic growth, promoting maximum employment and attaining stable prices. They also include reducing budget or balance of payment deficits and ensuring fair distribution of income.
Balance of trade is the difference between export and import of goods and services of a country for a given period.
Monetarists prescribe active fiscal policy to alleviate weak aggregate demand.
items.why: That is the Keynesian prescription. Monetarists favour monetary policy and a constant money-growth rule.

items.text: Which one of the following is not a macroeconomic question?
opts: What determines the level of economic activity in a society?
What determines how many goods and services a nation produces?
What determines how many jobs are available in an economy?
What causes a firm to grow?
items.ans: What causes a firm to grow?
items.why: The growth of a single firm is about one economic unit: microeconomics. The others are about national totals.

items.text: Technological change has the largest impact on which form of unemployment?
items.why: New technology changes the skills employers demand; workers with old skills become structurally unemployed until retrained.
items.clue: Skills no longer match the jobs.

items.text: If the national economy is closed, i.e. a country has no interaction with the rest of the world, then
items.why: GNP = GDP + NFI. In a closed economy no factor income flows in or out, so NFI = 0 and GNP = GDP.
items.clue: What is NFI with no foreign links?

items.text: Which one of the following refers to the recurrent ups and downs in the level of economic activity?
items.why: A boom and a trough are single points of one cycle; the whole up-and-down pattern is the business cycle.
items.clue: The whole pattern, not one point.

items.text: One of the following is not true about the evolution and recent development of macroeconomics.
opts: The classical view was the predominant economic philosophy until the Great Depression.
Keynesian economics is more useful for analysing the macroeconomy in the short run.
The most recent wave of new Keynesian economics is more micro-based.
Monetarists argued that it is fiscal policy and not monetary policy that addresses the macroeconomic problems.
items.ans: Monetarists argued that it is fiscal policy and not monetary policy that addresses the macroeconomic problems.
items.why: The book says the opposite: monetarists argued for MONETARY policy, not fiscal policy. The other three are true.

items.text: Economic growth is best measured by the rise in
opts: real GDP or real per capita income
items.ans: real GDP or real per capita income
items.why: Real values remove price changes; per capita values allow for population growth.

items.text: Which describes GNP rather than GDP?
opts: Output of a country's own factors of production, wherever located
Output produced within the country's borders
items.ans: Output of a country's own factors of production, wherever located
items.why: GDP is location-based; GNP is ownership-based: GNP = GDP + NFI.
